source.title: An Empirical Study of the Relation Between Network Architecture and Complexity

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied; it includes the proposal and reported results, with some figure text flattened.
record.tranche_reason: Tests model scaling as ImageNet class count increases, an extension to the claim’s capacity and generalization topic. It does not test the listed versions’ random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, or train-test gap.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the reported validation-accuracy results for model size versus class-count complexity. Figure 3 reports means and standard deviations; no exact plotted values are recoverable from the supplied text. The authors’ statements about memorization and generalization refer to cited Zhang et al. work, not a result tested here.
record.test_reason: The study measures validation accuracy while varying ResNet size and ImageNet class count. None of V1–V8 is tested: the width experiments do not establish zero training error or examine widening beyond interpolation. The authors invoke memorization and generalization from prior work without measuring random-label memorization themselves.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: accuracy declines approximately log-linearly with class count, and model scaling yields diminishing returns in this limited setting. The authors explicitly interpret their results as supporting earlier memorization/generalization findings, but their experiments do not establish the random-label comparison required by V1.
record.recipe_differences: Uses class-count complexity sweeps on ImageNet subsets and validation accuracy; the tested results use basic ResNets trained for 90 epochs with SGD, momentum and warm-up. It does not reproduce the claim’s random-label memorization or train-test-gap experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size changes accuracy; the slope of the log-linear accuracy trend depends on model size. Fixed versus increasing training sample count changes the tested setting. At fixed sample count, architectures begin to converge in a low-performance regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the tested basic ResNets, validation accuracy decreases approximately log-linearly with class count, while larger models improve accuracy. With 100,000 training examples held fixed, models begin converging toward a low-performance regime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested 90-epoch ImageNet-subset recipe, increasing ResNet depth or width improves validation accuracy across class counts, while increasing class count reduces accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: 2019 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshop (ICCVW)
record.problems: The experiment is limited to basic ResNet architectures and a single class ordering; some planned repetitions were not completed. Models were trained for only 90 epochs with a less robust hyperparameter search. The maximum 3,761 classes was insufficient to observe the proposed highest-complexity regime. Exact values are available only in figures, not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results omitted. Planned architecture comparisons were not completed; no results for vanilla CNN, ResNeXt, DenseNet, or other architectural innovations are reported.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Test-error behavior when widening beyond the width needed for zero training error, with training to convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects and recipe adaptations; all reported experiments use batch size 128.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reported scaling trends are valid descriptive findings; cannot_determine refers to their inability to establish any listed version. The random-classifier reference is chance accuracy for the natural-label task, not a network trained on random labels. The final experimental setup supersedes the preregistered Adam and early-stopping protocol.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare natural-label test accuracy with random-label chance performance.
Does not sweep width beyond the zero-training-error threshold or report test error in that setting.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks or isolate local connectivity.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
Does not vary batch size or measure a large-batch generalization penalty.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or relate it to the train-test gap.
Does not remove memorized examples or compare against random removals.
